=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of the Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold points**
- The Seller says these positions are "FINAL" and "settled at principal level". Nothing in the package evidences that. Please confirm with the deal principals before we treat anything as agreed. Our mark-up should reserve all positions.
- The Seller's "market" ranges are its own assertions and are unverified. Several of its positions are outside even the ranges it cites.
- The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the cover note. It admits no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay payment evidence, bonuses missing from the funds flow, and an unscoped incident. The cover note's reassurances should be disregarded where they conflict.
- The data room cut-off is 22 Sept 2026, so it is stale. Require a refreshed cut-off and disclosure against a fixed, agreed index.

The figures below are proposed opening positions for the team to calibrate, not market findings.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, with the cap applying to general warranties only.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at about 35–40% (AUD 8.4–9.6m) for general warranties and settle no lower than 25–30%. The Seller's 20% is acceptable only if the risks below are carved out and uncapped. Several known exposures (Bluefen, incident, Ironquay, tax) sit outside "general" and must not be squeezed under this cap.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis, plus an AUD 250,000 basket (about 1% of price) that is a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** Lower thresholds, a tipping (first-dollar) basket, and claims aggregated across related matters.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10,000 de minimis (with related claims aggregated) and a tipping basket of about AUD 120,000 (0.5%). A deductible basket on top of a de minimis shaves recoveries twice. Thresholds must not apply to fundamental, tax, fraud or specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months, so two audit cycles are covered. Longer periods for fundamental and tax warranties. The default should be reversed so limits apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties. The Seller's "applies to all unless stated" wording would silently cut off title, tax and indemnity claims, so reject it.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties capped and time-limited like general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate fundamental regime with a cap equal to 100% of price, no basket or de minimis, and a long tail (6 years or more).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title and capacity go to the root of what is being bought, and "simplicity" does not justify the Buyer losing protection if it does not receive 100% of the shares.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** None offered. The package is silent, and its limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that fraud, dishonest concealment and wilful misconduct (by the Seller or on its behalf) are uncapped and not time-barred. The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses should not apply to them.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on the carve-out. Do not rely on public policy to imply it, and keep the non-reliance clause from undermining misleading-conduct rights.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records, against all warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, fair and with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. No deemed disclosure of the data room or public records. Disclosure should not qualify indemnities, fundamental warranties or tax.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Limit it to the Disclosure Letter's specific items, and make sure the 1.4 "no admission" language cannot be used to argue the Buyer accepted the risks.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause so Buyer rights are unaffected by knowledge or investigation. At most, actual knowledge of named individuals about a specific fact.
- **Recommendation:** Delete. Combined with general disclosure, this would give the Seller a defence to nearly every claim, and it would catch the known issues the Buyer is trying to price or indemnify.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Buyer wants:** A hard condition precedent to Completion, benefiting the Buyer only, and waivable only by it. The consent must be unconditional, or any clause 11.3 conditions must be satisfied. It must be in agreed form with no adverse amendments. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or 30%, of FY26 revenue.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "treated as satisfied" mechanic. The Disclosure Letter admits no consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists. Consider a price adjustment or termination right if consent is not delivered, and cover any consent costs.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion". About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and unrepaid.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment at Completion out of the proceeds. That means a payout letter, a funds-flow line, and discharge of all security delivered on payment. This follows from the debt-free/cash-free basis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. Deduct the payout amount from the price and require simultaneous discharge. Check whether the security includes a share charge, since that also affects title (see N-015).

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** Treatment as debt-like or transaction costs, deducted from the price, plus on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax), which the Disclosure Letter does not quantify.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct AUD 420,000 plus on-costs from the price, or have the Seller fund them at Completion. If left with the Company, they are a Buyer cost, which breaches the debt-free principle.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** SOW3 fees paid and cleared before Completion, with a confirmatory IP assignment delivered. The indemnity should cover loss from any defect in ownership of the Project Materials, including third-party claims and remediation. The indemnity should sit outside the cap, basket and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as adequate. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of the Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and no receipt or assignment is in the data room. Make payment and assignment a Completion deliverable.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity, outside the caps and thresholds, for investigation, notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party costs. Add a retention or escrow, cooperation and conduct-of-claims rights, and a specific warranty on privacy compliance.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "not material". The Disclosure Letter itself says about 1,240 personal records may be involved and that access, scope and notification obligations are unknown. Do not close while those are unknown unless the risk is ring-fenced.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The contracts and a Seller explanation of when each was committed, whether it is terminable, and what period it covers.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence. The Disclosure Letter does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. If they were committed pre-Completion, or cover periods before it, treat them as a debt-like or working-capital adjustment. Add a covenant against new commitments before Completion.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One undifferentiated regime ("all Claims", "same caps and time limits").
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for (a) general warranties, (b) fundamental/title, (c) tax, (d) specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, others), (e) fraud and wilful misconduct, and (f) covenants and price adjustments.
- **Recommendation:** Make this a structural point of our mark-up. Each category gets its own cap, thresholds and period, and limitation clauses apply only where expressly stated.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** DD-012, the Company's own share register, evidences title to 100% of the shares. The Disclosure Letter says this does not mean the Buyer has completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC searches, issue and transfer history, constitution and shareholder agreements, and PPSR and security searches. Add an unencumbered-title warranty, and at Completion delivery of signed transfers, share certificates and security releases.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. A company register is self-reported, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares. Make the verification a condition and keep the title warranty fundamental.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone tax indemnity or deed that is pre-Completion focused, outside the basket, with a long tail (at least the amendment period plus a buffer, about 6 years). IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, open-source and contractor assignments, treated as a more protected category.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Nothing in the package shows tax or IP positions were negotiated, and the Ironquay and incident issues show IP and data risk is live. Keep tax and IP outside the general regime until diligence on both is complete.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Confirm with principals whether anything was actually agreed at principal level.
2. Make Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment and assignment, and bonus funding conditions or Completion deliverables, with a revised funds flow.
3. Request a refreshed data room cut-off plus the missing documents: Bluefen consent, Sandbar contracts, Ironquay payment evidence, and incident investigation findings.
4. Reserve the Buyer's price position. The items in N-009, N-010, N-013 and possibly N-008 together are around AUD 4m or more of price impact before any damages exposure.
